definition: Predicting a person’s ongoing or upcoming activity from sensor or video data — anticipation rather than just recognition.
details: Predicting a person’s ongoing or upcoming activity from sensor or video data — anticipation rather than just recognition.

explainer.lead: Activity prediction uses video or sensor readings to work out what someone is doing now or is about to do next. It matters when a system needs to respond early, rather than waiting until an action is complete.

tiers.eli5: It is like seeing a friend pick up a ball and guessing that they are about to throw it. A computer looks for clues in camera images or wearable sensors, then makes its best guess before the whole activity happens.
tiers.practitioner: An application processes a recent window of video or sensor data and outputs a current or future activity, often with a confidence score. Useful systems account for incomplete observations, sensor noise, and actions whose early stages look alike; confidence should not be treated as certainty.
tiers.paperLevel: Given observations x_1:t from video or sensors, estimate the ongoing activity y_t or an upcoming activity y_t+k before it is fully observed. The task is anticipatory rather than purely retrospective, and predictions can be unreliable when early cues are weak or several activities share the same beginning.

explainer.example: A camera observes someone walking toward a door and reaching for its handle. The system predicts “opening the door” before the door has moved, allowing a response based on that anticipated activity.

usedIn.name: Human–robot interaction
usedIn.detail: Anticipating a person’s next action so a robot can respond earlier.

usedIn.name: Assistive technology
usedIn.detail: Inferring an ongoing or upcoming activity to provide timely assistance.

usedIn.name: Wearable monitoring
usedIn.detail: Using sensor readings to anticipate what the wearer is about to do.

usedIn.name: Video analytics
usedIn.detail: Forecasting activities from partially observed video sequences.

explainer.intuition: Many activities give clues before they are complete. Activity prediction uses those clues to look ahead, while activity recognition mainly labels what has already been observed.
howItWorks: Collect recent video frames or sensor readings.
Extract cues about the person’s movement and situation.
Compare those cues with patterns associated with different activities.
Estimate the current or upcoming activity and, where available, its confidence.
explainer.whyItMatters: Prediction gives systems time to respond before an activity finishes. This anticipatory ability is useful when waiting for a complete action would make the response too late.
misconceptions: It is not simply activity recognition: recognition labels observed behavior, while prediction includes anticipating what comes next.
A prediction is not a certainty, especially when different activities begin with similar movements.
It does not reveal a person’s intentions beyond what can be inferred from the available observations.

diagram.caption: Partial video or sensor observations are turned into a prediction before the activity is complete.
